Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Fourth seed Elena Dementieva avoided an embarrassing early exit when comeback queen Jelena Dokic's French Open hopes were ended by a back injury on Thursday. Jelena Dokic was left in tears after being forced to retire hurt against Elena Dementieva at the French Open. Dokic, taking part in her first French Open since 2004 following well-documented family problems, won the first set 6-2 and -- after her first break for treatment -- broke the 2004 finalist to lead 3-2 in their second round clash. But the Russian won the next two games as the tearful former world No.4 was reduced to walking pace before calling it quits. "I went for a return and I just went down and couldn't get back up," she said. "It's very painful and very disappointing because I felt as if I had the match in my hands." Dokic, now ranked 80th after reviving her career with a run to the quarter-finals of the Australian Open in January, had won her opening match on Tuesday when she came back from a set down to beat Slovenia's Karolina Sprem 3-6 6-1 6-2. The 26-year-old's career had nosedived following her highly-publicized split from controversial mentor and father Damir. Dementieva will next play Australian 30th seed Samantha Stosur, who won her second-round match in straight sets against Belgium's Yanina Wickmayer. Earlier on Thursday, the Williams sisters also progressed through to the third round with contrasting victories. Second seed Serena crushed Virginia Ruano Pascual 6-2 6-0 to set up a clash with another unseeded Spaniard, Maria Jose Martinez Sanchez. Third seed Venus survived a scare against unseeded Czech Lucie Safarova before completing a match that was halted on Wednesday night due to bad light. The American saved a match point at 5-4 down in the third set before managing to hold, break her opponent and then serve out to love for a 6-7 (5-7) 6-2 7-5 success. Venus, who lost the 2002 final to Serena, will next play Hungarian 29th seed Agnes Szavay. Fifth seed Jelena Jankovic had no such troubles in beating Magdalena Rybarikova of Slovakia 6-1 6-2, setting up a third-round clash with unseeded Austrian Jarmila Groth. Seventh-seeded Russian Svetlana Kuznetsova also advanced along with Danish 10th seed Caroline Wozniacki, but 13th seed Marion Bartoli of France made a surprise exit. The 2007 Wimbledon finalist lost 6-3 7-5 to Tathiana Garbin of Italy, who will next take on unseeded Virginie Razzano of France.

## French Open match report: Dokic comeback halted by injury against Dementieva

Jelena Dokic’s stirring comeback story took a painful turn at Roland Garros when she was forced to retire injured against fourth seed Elena Dementieva in the second round of the French Open.

Dokic, who had been one of the most compelling stories in women’s tennis after her emotional resurgence at the Australian Open earlier in the season, had looked on course for another significant result. The Australian started superbly against Dementieva, taking the opening set 6-2 with clean, aggressive hitting and the sort of fearless baseline tennis that had once carried her into the world’s top 10.

But with the match poised in the second set, Dokic’s movement deteriorated sharply because of a back/lower-body injury. Dementieva had edged ahead 4-3 in the second set when Dokic, visibly distressed and unable to continue properly, retired. The official scoreline read: **Dementieva defeated Dokic 2-6, 4-3 retired**.

### Dokic starts brilliantly

For much of the opening set, Dokic was the better player. She took the ball early, attacked Dementieva’s second serve and repeatedly pushed the Russian behind the baseline. Dementieva, one of the game’s best athletes and a former French Open finalist, struggled to settle as Dokic dictated with flat, penetrating groundstrokes.

Dokic’s timing was especially impressive given the setting and the opponent. She had come into Roland Garros still rebuilding her ranking and confidence, but for a set she looked like the player who had once beaten elite opponents on the sport’s biggest stages.

### Injury changes the match

The tone shifted in the second set. Dokic began showing clear signs of discomfort, particularly between points and when stretching wide. Her serve lost pace, her court coverage became restricted, and Dementieva began to find more rhythm as the rallies lengthened.

At 3-4 in the second set, Dokic could no longer continue. The retirement was a cruel end to a match in which she had given herself a real chance of upsetting one of the tournament’s leading seeds.

Dementieva advanced, but the focus afterward was largely on Dokic’s misfortune. The Russian had survived a difficult assignment, yet the match never reached a natural conclusion because of the injury.

## Background: Dokic’s comeback story

Dokic’s appearance at the French Open came during one of the most emotional comeback seasons in recent tennis memory.

A former Wimbledon semifinalist and world No. 4, Dokic had spent years away from the top level amid injuries, loss of form and well-documented personal difficulties. Her return to prominence at the **2009 Australian Open** was one of that tournament’s defining narratives. Backed by a passionate home crowd, she won several dramatic matches and reached the quarterfinals, her deepest Grand Slam run in years.

That Melbourne run reintroduced Dokic as a serious competitor and reminded the tennis world of her ball-striking ability, resilience and fighting spirit. Roland Garros was supposed to be another step in that rebuilding process. Instead, the retirement against Dementieva underlined how fragile comebacks can be, especially for players trying to regain elite fitness after long and difficult spells away from the top tier.

- **Serena Williams** moved through comfortably, producing a dominant display and reinforcing her status as one of the title contenders despite clay not being her most successful surface.

- **Dinara Safina**, the world No. 1 at the time, also advanced impressively. Safina had entered the tournament under pressure to justify her top ranking with a first Grand Slam title, and her early-round form was commanding.

- **Maria Sharapova**, still working her way back after shoulder problems, battled through another test. Her return was being closely watched, and although she was not yet back to her most dominant level, her competitiveness remained unmistakable.

- **Svetlana Kuznetsova**, a former US Open champion and always dangerous on clay, progressed with a solid performance. Her heavy forehand and experience made her one of the players to watch in Paris.

- **Ana Ivanovic**, the defending champion, remained in the spotlight as she attempted to recapture the form that had taken her to the Roland Garros title the previous year.

- **Victoria Azarenka** continued to build momentum as part of the younger group of contenders trying to break deeper into the Grand Slam conversation.

The day’s results kept the top half of the women’s draw largely on course, but Dokic’s retirement was one of the more emotional moments. What had begun as a potential upset over Dementieva ended instead with an injury-enforced exit, leaving Dokic to hope that her comeback would not be derailed for long.
